links.note: A frozen-model explanation audit compares the readout's stated importance against the behaviour it purports to explain.
Controlled perturbations compare attribution-predicted effects with actual score changes, conditional on the perturbation design.
Calibration measures quantify the discrepancy between predicted probabilities and observed frequencies in a specified population.
Scope: explanation-specific metrics, which quantify agreement between attributed importance and responses under a defined perturbation distribution.
Blinded clinical review can assess whether an explanation looks reasonable for the task, separately from computational testing.
Calibration can be assessed within prespecified patient or acquisition groups; this does not establish fairness under every criterion.
An audit can compare frozen-model probabilities with independently obtained outcomes on a declared evaluation population.
Shortcut hypotheses are explicit audit targets requiring task-specific investigation, not aggregate accuracy.
Controlled changes to suspected non-diagnostic cues reveal predictor sensitivity; shown on COVID-19 radiograph classifiers, not gallbladder models.
Generative comparisons can expose candidate cues, but coupled edits prevent treating each comparison as an isolated intervention.
An explicit causal model identifies candidate confounding paths relative to an estimand; it does not discover unmeasured confounders.
Causal analysis separates an observed association from the intervention claim it might be taken to support.
Stratifying by suspected cue availability can reveal shortcut-compatible failures; severity and case-mix remain alternative explanations.
Attributions nominate suspicious regions for controlled testing; they do not independently establish reliance.
A common-cause pathway produces association that does not represent the causal effect being estimated.
An association available in training can support a rule that fails when it changes; learning that rule is not inevitable.
Learned representations can privilege easy predictive cues over the evidence the task intends.
Acquisition and documentation workflows can couple annotations with the target imaged; demonstrated on fetal-ultrasound calipers.
Removing or replacing regions at test time creates inputs unlike training data; ROAR answers this by retraining, which changes the question.
Moving a model from referred symptomatic patients into screening changes eligibility, prevalence and disease spectrum.
Moving between institutions changes acquisition and patient distributions, as shown for pneumonia models across hospitals.
Observed morphology and acoustic findings feed task-specific reasoning without determining the diagnosis alone.
A matched tissue result can be incorporated while retaining specimen, sampling and timing limits.
CT/MRI observations contribute when they address the unresolved clinical question.
Independently assessed findings can anchor an ultrasound evidence audit; annotations derived from the explanation would be circular.
Matched tissue diagnoses support outcome verification but cannot substitute for annotations of image-visible evidence.
Independently annotated sonographic findings can be operationalised as concepts, given validated measurement and separation.
Adequately acquired ultrasound supplies diagnostically relevant gallbladder observations.
Findings such as intramural cystic spaces support particular differentials; no generic feature establishes every disease.
Scope: malignancy-risk assessment of gallbladder polyps. Morphology and size inform risk, not a pathological stage.
Appropriately sampled tissue establishes malignant histology and sampled invasion, not necessarily the complete stage.
CT/MRI supplies evidence about tumour extent and spread, with limits for microscopic disease.
Scope: MRCP assessment of ductal configuration, narrowing and filling defects; these do not alone determine cause.
Ultrasound supplies observations of parenchyma and the visible hepatobiliary system, subject to acoustic access.
Scope: CT/MRI in stroke assessment, including haemorrhage or ischaemic injury; not every neurological diagnosis.
A matched specimen provides tissue-level evidence for the sampled lesion; surgical selection limits generalisation.
Applicable guidelines specify how defined findings and risk factors inform a decision; the example is polyp management.
A screening guideline supplies eligibility and follow-up rules against which a workflow can be specified and audited.
Scope: diagnostic-accuracy components. STARD specifies reporting of participants, reference procedures and analysis.
Reporting requires specified estimates and their precision; compliance does not make a metric appropriate for every claim.
Calibration established on one distribution need not persist on another, so reassessment is warranted.
Shift motivates checking uncertainty quality and the risk and coverage of any acceptance policy.
Changed populations or acquisition conditions require reassessing subgroup performance; aggregate results cannot answer it.
A visually convincing explanation can be insensitive to learned parameters, so reasonableness does not entail faithfulness.
A faithful explanation of caliper reliance accurately describes an inappropriate rule without making it clinically plausible.
Agreement between probabilities and outcome frequencies does not constrain whether an explanation describes the predictor.
Scope: predictive-performance metrics such as AUROC. They describe predictions against labels, not the computation.
Localisation or mask overlap does not establish that an explanation identifies the evidence a diagnostic predictor used.
A tissue diagnosis does not establish that a finding was visible or assessable in the frame supplied to the model.
A compliant report can describe a method whose faithfulness claim remains unsupported.
An adapted instance can be frozen and audited for its evidence use; pretraining scale is not an exemption.
Representations can be inspected for encoded clinical and acquisition information, keeping decodability separate from reliance.
Segmentation outputs can be audited for dependence on documentation cues.
Parameter and label randomisation test whether attribution outputs respond to the learned predictor at all.
Audit the concept examples, held-out measurement quality, correlated concepts and claimed sensitivity.
Inspect whether an edited comparison changes its intended target while preserving other evidence.
Acquisition modes alter acoustic findings; spatial compounding changed shadow appearance in a stone phantom.
Masking can erase diagnostically relevant morphology as well as the suspected nuisance cue.

types.Method: An analytical technique, learning procedure, or organised clinical or audit workflow.
types.Metric: A family of numerical evaluation measures.
types.Property: A characteristic assessed for a specified model, explanation, or population.
types.Threat: A mechanism or condition that can compromise an evidential inference or its transportability.
types.ClinicalTarget: The clinical question or domain for which evidence is being assessed.
types.EvidenceSource: An acquisition or examination process whose observations can supply evidence.
types.Finding: A family of observations interpretable from an examination or image.
types.Standard: A normative document specifying clinical or reporting requirements.
types.ModelFamily: A family of trained computational systems.

relations.assessesProperty: Provides a procedure or numerical assessment of the property, without establishing it conclusively.
relations.probesThreat: Can investigate a hypothesis about the threat; nominating a candidate is not confirming a mechanism.
relations.canIntroduce: Can create or enable the object. Neither inevitability nor sufficient causation is implied.
relations.usesEvidence: Observations from the object enter the subject's assessment or reasoning.
relations.providesEvidenceFor: Can supply observations bearing on the clinical question, without alone resolving it.
relations.constrainsProcedure: Specifies decision rules or reporting requirements. Compliance is not guaranteed.
relations.warrantsReassessmentOf: Gives reason to reassess; does not assert that anything has deteriorated.
relations.doesNotEstablish: The subject alone is insufficient to establish the object. Non-entailment, not incompatibility.
relations.canAudit: Instances or outputs of the object can be explicit inspection targets of the subject.
relations.changesObservabilityOf: Can change the visibility or assessability of findings without a change in underlying disease.
